toyota_summary:
China laid out a concrete proposal at the International Maritime Organization for shipping decarbonization rules, positioning itself as a moderate between stricter European proposals and looser alternatives. The move matters because maritime shipping moves roughly 90 percent of global auto trade, and Chinese leverage over these standards affects how much automakers will pay to transport vehicles and parts across oceans. Watch whether Europe accepts China's middle ground or pushes back in the next negotiating round in November.

Germany will present its position on China trade policy to the EU by October, likely pushing for tougher measures. This directly shapes tariff exposure and supply-chain risk for any automaker sourcing batteries, semiconductors, or components from China or selling finished vehicles there. The outcome will become clearer once Berlin's formal proposal hits Brussels next month.

emails.excerpt: ドイツ政府は10月までにEUに対し、中国との貿易政策をより厳しくするための提案を提示する予
emails.subject_en: Germany to set position on EU-China trade in October, Merz says
emails.summary_en: Germany plans to present a unified, tougher stance on EU-China trade policy by October, ahead of an EU summit where negotiators will report on efforts to shrink the bloc's massive trade deficit with Beijing. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said his coalition is compiling proposals as German industry groups, including automotive and machinery sectors, reassess their China strategies. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said Germany remains committed to free trade but will not be naive about rule-breaking by trading partners.
emails.summary_ja: ドイツ政府は10月までにEUの対中貿易政策について、より強硬な統一見解をまとめる方針だ。10月のEUサミットでは中国との巨額の貿易赤字削減に向けた交渉状況が報告される予定で、メルツ首相は自動車・機械業界を含む産業界からも対中姿勢の見直しが進んでいると述べた。クリングバイル財務相は、自由貿易を引き続き重視する一方、ルールを破る相手に対しては甘い対応をしないと強調した。
